The patient's 12-year contact with mental health services was characterised by shifting diagnostic labels that reflected clinicians’ focus on presenting symptom fluctuations rather than the underlying chronic depressive baseline.

She described her care as “changing medications without changing anything about how I feel,” which led her to request escalation to higher-intensity interventions such as ketamine therapy or electroconvulsive therapy.
No structured follow-up occurred, as the patient subsequently disengaged from services consistent with her long-standing pattern of treatment fatigue in the context of chronic depressive illness.

summary.text: A 48-year-old single woman presented with lifelong pervasive low mood, anhedonia, low self-esteem and passive death wishes, with a chronic depressive baseline since adolescence. She denied suicidal intent or planning and neurovegetative symptoms, kept stable employment and independent living, and had no self-harm, impulsivity or crisis-driven service use. She had no family history of mental illness and a medical history of lumbar disc prolapse.

Full blood count, thyroid function tests, metabolic profile and B12/folate were within normal limits, with no clinical or biochemical evidence of a contributing medical or neurological condition; collateral history from family was unavailable.

Over 12 years the recorded diagnosis shifted from MDD (2012) to RDD with GAD (2014-2017), EUPD (2017-2018), MDD with GAD and "EUPD traits" (2020-2023) and RDD again (2024). Treatment trials by period included sertraline, fluoxetine, escitalopram, venlafaxine, sodium valproate, olanzapine, dothiepin and quetiapine augmentation, plus a full course of DBT, with minimal sustained improvement. The authors state that structured longitudinal assessment and scale-based monitoring were absent during this period.

The authors revised the diagnosis to persistent depressive disorder with intermittent major depressive episodes, without current episode (Type 3), based on longitudinal assessment. The patient had treatment fatigue, requested ketamine or ECT, and disengaged from services shortly after the revised diagnosis with no structured follow-up.
